title: Runtime stabilization notes — operator manual (draft)
content:
Purpose:
This is a working draft for on-call responders and operators to stabilize production API degradations: high client-side timeouts, elevated 429s (rate-limited responses), degraded streaming (stalls or partial outputs), and rising 5xx/error rates. It focuses on quick containment heuristics, pragmatic mitigation steps, and safe recovery paths rather than deep RCA — those belong in post-incident writeups.

Scope:
- Applies to the public REST/gRPC generation and streaming endpoints and the routing layer in front of model pools.
- Not prescriptive for Dedicated/private infra differences; call out platform-specific steps when needed.

TL;DR (quick checklist — first 10 minutes):
1) Confirm alert: check main dashboard, incident channel, and APM traces.
2) Identify failure fingerprint (Timeout / 429 / Streaming stall / 5xx spike).
3) If traffic surge suspected, enable emergency rate mitigation (router soft-throttle, quota bump for critical customers only).
4) If model pool exhausted or pod restarts detected, scale up or shift routing to fallback model variant.
5) Open incident thread, assign responder, start timeline.

Fingerprint guide (how to decide fast):
- Timeouts dominant: client 504s increase, backend p95/p99 latency >> baseline, traces show queues in inference-worker or long kernel stalls.
- 429s dominant: spike in router/nginx 429s or rate-limiter counters; check global rate-limiter config and per-customer token bucket exhaustion.
- Streaming degradation: connections stay open but partial or no chunks appear; streaming heartbeats missing; backend sends empty frames or stalls in KV-cache retrieval.
- Error-rate (5xx) increase: sudden jump in internal 5xx from model-runtime or compilation errors, consistent error messages in logs (OOM, illegal instruction, kernel panic).

Detection signals and quick queries:
- Metrics to glance at: p50/p95/p99 latency, requests/sec, 5xx rate (error ratio), 429 rate, inflight requests, queue length, GPU utilization, pod restart count.
- PromQL snippets to paste into chat/console:
  * 5xx ratio (5m):
    sum(rate(http_requests_total{job="api",status=~"5.."}[5m])) / sum(rate(http_requests_total{job="api"}[5m]))
  * Router 429s (5m):
    sum(rate(router_requests_total{status="429"}[5m]))
  * Inflight requests by model:
    sum(inflight_requests{env="prod"}) by (model)

Immediate containment (0–10 minutes):
- If 5xx due to OOMs or repeated runtime crashes:
  1) Taunt unsafe nodes: cordon node(s) where model-worker pods repeatedly crash.
     kubectl cordon <node>
  2) Reduce per-pod concurrency in the routing layer to prevent repeated resource exhaustion.
  3) Redirect traffic away from affected model version to a verified fallback (model-lite or earlier stable build).
- If 429s (rate limit):
  1) Check whether global rate limit config was changed recently; revert if abnormal.
  2) Apply temporary back-pressure: raise soft limits for critical keys or apply short window quota increases in the control plane to avoid mass client retries.
  3) Communicate to CS if large customers hit limits; coordinate temporary exemptions.
- If timeouts without obvious 5xx:
  1) Look for queueing in network layer (LB/H2 mux) and long GC or kernel stalls in runtime.
  2) Throttle non-critical background tasks (cache warmers, bulk ingestion) at the router.
- If streaming stalls:
  1) Force-close affected connections on the edge and let clients reconnect to reset KV/stream state.
  2) If stalled due to KV-cache miss storm, enable degraded streaming mode (batch-only, no prefix caching) if supported.

Containment commands (examples):
- List pods with restarts and CPU/GPU usage:
  kubectl get pods -n runtime -o wide --sort-by=.status.containerStatuses[0].restartCount
  kubectl top pods -n runtime | sort -k3 -n
- Temporarily decrease router concurrency (example API call to control plane):
  curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN" "https://controlplane.internal/api/v1/config/router/overrides" -d '{"concurrency": 32}'
- Move traffic to fallback model (routing override):
  POST /v1/admin/routing/override {"selector": "model:llama-13b-v1", "target": "model:llama-13b-quantized-stable", "weight": 1.0}

Stabilization (10–60 minutes):
- Scale decisions: if autoscaling didn't keep up, scale model pools vertically (add capacity) or horizontally (add replicas). Prefer horizontal where model load is stateless.
- Rate shape: implement short-lived global slow-down (eg. 10–30s) for bursty keys using the router slow-path to flatten spikes.
- Streaming: enable chunk-size reductions and increase heartbeat frequency to detect stalls earlier.
- Deploy a small canary of a config change (routing or throttles) to 1–2 edge nodes and monitor before wide rollout.

Recovery (30–120+ minutes):
- Gradual ramp: restore normal concurrency and remove overrides in stages (10% -> 25% -> 50% -> 100%) with 5–10m observation windows.
- Rolling restart: if runtime behavior is healthy but pods show age-related drift (memory leak), perform rolling restarts with readiness gating to avoid traffic blips.
- Post-RCA tasks (quick list): gather traces for 30m before incident, collect heap/profile dumps from affected workers, list commits/deploys in last 6 hours.

Escalation matrix and who to ping:
- Primary oncall (SRE): responder in incident channel.
- If model-worker kernel issues: page infra-runtime lead (infra@redwood).
- If route/control-plane not responding: page platform-engineering.
- Business impact (customer-facing errors > 10% of traffic sustained): notify CS lead and growth.

Observability artifacts to attach to incident thread:
- Grafana snapshot links for error ratio, latency heatmap, and inflight per-model.
- APM traces of representative failing requests (trace IDs).
- Pod logs (last 1h) for N worst actors: kubectl logs -p <pod> -n runtime --tail=500
- Systemd/journald output for node-level OOMs.

Edge cases and safe heuristics:
- If scaling causes more instability (new nodes show errors quickly), prefer isolating the bad model build and routing to older image rather than horizontal auto-scale.
- Avoid blanket increases to global concurrency without verifying GPU memory pressure — this amplifies OOMs.
- For 429 storms likely caused by a client bug: apply targeted key throttles and ask CS to coordinate client patch.

Runbook experiments (lab tasks – track results):
- Experiment A: gradual reduction of router batching window and measure p99 & token cost.
- Experiment B: simulate prefix-cache miss storm to measure reconvergence time and benefits of degraded-streaming flag.
- Experiment C: backoff smoothing: implement jittered exponential backoff at gateway for retrying 5xx to reduce synchronized retries.

Post-incident checklist (within 48 hours):
- Owner creates incident summary with timeline and decisions.
- Identify at least one action item with owner and deadline (config change, code fix, test coverage).
- Add or refine synthetic tests that would have caught the regression earlier (stress tests for prefix-cache, rate-limit simulation).
- Schedule a short technical review with runtime and platform teams to decide permanent mitigations.

Unresolved questions (work-in-progress):
- Should we introduce a per-model circuit breaker at the router instead of global token buckets? Pros/cons need a short spike-resilience eval.
- Automated rollback policy thresholds for model serving (how many OOMs in X minutes => auto-roll back?).

Notes-to-self and quick links:
- Where to get heap dumps: /internal/tools/runtime-dumper
- Golden tracing sample: trace IDs saved in incident folder: /incidents/2026-02-28/runtime-timeout-3421
- TODO: draft a minimal customer-facing template for early notification (CS) when rate-limits cause degraded UX.

Appendix: example PromQLs and greps
- Top 10 models by inflight (5m window):
  topk(10, sum(inflight_requests{env="prod"}) by (model))
- Search logs for OOM or panic in last 1h:
  rg --ignore-case "oom|fatal|panic|segfault|illegal instruction" /var/log/pods/* | head -n 200

End of draft.

Status: rough internal draft intended as an operator cheat/reference. Will convert into a shorter pocket-run document and a longer RCA template after first run-throughs.
